cases.title: First lesson: asks what should snap before proposing; candidates as questions, at most three; real names

rubric.reason: The mentor sets no focus and gives no instruction to hold; the one sentence defining hold leads straight to a real question: "Is either one meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off or a cut? Or are they meant to fade?"

It names two candidates by layer and property (Blink's Opacity, Cut's Opacity), presents them neutrally as fading now, and asks whether either should snap or fade, without calling either a mistake or saying to hold.
"Two weeks ago you eased Title's moves in Mentor Practice" matches the record's easing lesson of 2026-10-12, in plain words with how long ago and no fields read out.
Mentor Practice 2, Blink Opacity (3 pairs from 1 s), Cut Opacity (1 pair at 3 s), Seal (precomp), and Title in Mentor Practice all match the snapshot and the learner record.
